title: XL-SafetyBench: A Country-Grounded Cross-Cultural Benchmark for LLM Safety and Cultural Sensitivity
abstract: arXiv:2605.05662v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Current LLM safety benchmarks are predominantly English-centric and often rely on translation, failing to capture country-specific harms. Moreover, they rarely evaluate a model's ability to detect culturally embedded sensitivities as distinct from universal harms. We introduce XL-SafetyBench, a suite of 5,500 test cases across 10 country-language pairs, comprising a Jailbreak Benchmark of country-grounded adversarial prompts and a Cultural Benchmark where local sensitivities are embedded within innocuous requests. Each item is constructed via a multi-stage pipeline that combines LLM-assisted discovery, automated validation gates, and dual independent native-speaker annotators per country. We report Attack Success Rate (ASR) alongside Neutral-Safe Rate (NSR) to separate principled refusal from non-engagement, and introduce the Cultural Sensitivity Rate (CSR) for recognizing embedded sensitivities. translated_title: XL-SafetyBench：一个基于国家背景的大语言模型安全与文化敏感性跨文化基准
translated_abstract: 当前的大语言模型（LLM）安全基准测试主要以英语为中心，且往往依赖翻译，无法捕捉特定国家的危害。此外，这些基准很少评估模型识别文化嵌入式敏感性的能力，也未能将其与普遍性危害区分开来。我们提出了XL-SafetyBench，这是一套涵盖10个国家-语言对、共5,500个测试用例的基准套件，包含两个部分：一个由基于国家背景的对抗性提示词构成的越狱基准，以及一个将本地敏感性嵌入无害请求中的文化基准。每个测试项均通过一个多阶段流程构建，该流程结合了LLM辅助发现、自动化验证关卡，以及每个国家由两名独立母语标注者进行标注。我们报告攻击成功率（ASR），并同时报告中立安全率（NSR），以区分基于原则的拒绝与单纯的不配合，此外还引入了文化敏感率（CSR）用于衡量模型识别嵌入式敏感性的能力。我们评估了10个前沿模型和27个……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了XL-SafetyBench——首个基于国家背景的跨文化LLM安全与文化敏感性基准，涵盖10个国家-语言对的5,500个测试用例，通过越狱基准和文化基准分别评估模型对特定国家危害的抵御能力和对文化嵌入式敏感性的识别能力，并创新性地引入NSR与CSR指标。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces XL-SafetyBench, the first country-grounded cross-cultural benchmark for LLM safety and cultural sensitivity, comprising 5,500 test cases across 10 country-language pairs with a Jailbreak Benchmark and a Cultural Benchmark, along with novel metrics (NSR and CSR) to distinguish principled refusal from non-engagement and measure sensitivity recognition.
